transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not wasting your time today. 

Um, well, I'm mostly here because my wife asked me to come. I don't think it's anything too terrible, honestly, but... well, I've been putting together a memorial for my brother. I just want to do right by him, you know? I'm sure you can understand wanting to honor family. 

But I guess it’s gotten a little bit bigger than I originally meant it to. I’ve been spending most of my days just... chasing down the right songs, calling up folks, planning out these displays and a few trips for it. It's a good project, but my wife says I’ve completely pushed aside the garden, my walking group, and just about everything else lately. I just got a little wrapped up in making it nice, I think. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this the right way for you.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things that usually make you happy, like your garden or walking group, since you started working on this memorial project?

Oh, no, doctor, it's not... I wouldn't say I'm not enjoying them. I still love my garden, I really do. And the walking group is a wonderful bunch of fellas. I just... well, I guess I just haven't had the time? 

Or, I suppose I've just been so focused on making this memorial absolutely perfect that I just haven't gotten around to my usual hobbies. It's definitely not that I don't like them anymore. I just have my hands full right now trying to do a good job for my brother. I fully intend to get right back to the tomatoes and the morning walks once this is all sorted out and done right. 

I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm just abandoning my responsibilities or anything bad like that. I really am usually very good about keeping up with my routine. Does that make sense? Am I explaining that okay for you?
Have you noticed any days where even the thought of working in your garden or going for a walk doesn't bring you any sense of enjoyment or satisfaction?

Oh, I see what you're asking. No, doctor, I haven't really had any days quite like that. 

Even when I'm, you know, just up to my ears in making phone calls and arranging things for my brother, if I look out the window at the yard, I still get a real warm feeling thinking about it. I still get a lot of satisfaction just imagining getting my hands back in the dirt. It's just... well, there are only so many hours in the day right now, you know? 

But the thought of it still makes me happy, absolutely. I haven't lost my love for those things at all. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture here, I'd hate to mislead you or give the wrong impression. Am I doing okay answering your questions?
Have you felt down, sad, or hopeless at any point while working on this memorial project, even when things were going well?

Oh, no... no, doctor, I wouldn't say that at all. Honestly, I haven't felt down or hopeless in the slightest. 

I know it’s a memorial, and... well, I suppose people usually expect you to be very sad or weepy about these things, but I've actually been feeling quite alright. Really good, even! Just very driven to get it done right for him. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound cold or uncaring, saying I haven't been sad lately. I just... I really want to celebrate him, you know? Keep his memory alive in a beautiful way. So, no, no feelings of hopelessness or anything dark like that. I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need, and I'd hate for you to think I'm handling this poorly.
Have you found yourself not caring as much about your usual activities — like your garden or your walking group — even when you’re not working on the memorial?

Well, goodness, no, doctor. I certainly haven't stopped caring about them. Even on the rare occasion I step away from the memorial plans to just sit and have a cup of coffee, I'm still... well, I'm still looking out at the yard, planning where the new marigolds will go. And I still care very much about the walking group fellas, I really do. 

I'd hate for you to think I'm just turning my back on my life or my friends. That would be awful, wouldn't it? I still care deeply about all of it. I'm just temporarily preoccupied, I suppose you could say. Does that answer your question alright? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information, doctor.
On a day when you're not working on the memorial, have you noticed any decrease in how much enjoyment or interest you take in your garden or walking group when you actually do them?

Oh, goodness, no. No, doctor, I wouldn't say there's been any decrease at all. 

When I actually do get out there, you know, when I finally take a moment to prune the roses or catch up with the guys on a walk, it's just as wonderful as it's always been. Maybe even a little better, honestly, because it feels like a nice little break. I still get a tremendous amount of joy out of it. 

I really don't want you to worry that I'm losing interest in things or... or becoming depressed or anything like that. I'm still very much myself, just... busy, you know? I hope I'm making sense. Is that the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering everything correctly for you.
Have you had any days recently where, even when you're not working on the memorial, you just don't feel like doing your usual activities and they don't seem as enjoyable as they used to be?

Well, I know you're just being very thorough, doctor, and I really do appreciate that, but... honestly, no. I haven't had any days like that at all. 

I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or just brush off your questions. I'm really thinking hard about it because I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. But even when I take a breather from the memorial, I still want to be out doing my usual things. The garden still calls to me, and I still look forward to seeing the fellas. I haven't lost my taste for any of it, not for a single day. 

I hope it's alright that my answer is still no? I'd hate for you to think I'm hiding something or not taking this seriously. I'm just trying my best to be helpful and give you the honest truth. Am I doing okay with these questions, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you.
How long have you been focusing most of your time and energy on planning this memorial for your brother?

Well, let's see... it's been about two months now. Yes, right around two months. 

It started just after he passed, you see. I just... I felt this overwhelming need to make sure he was remembered properly, so I began working on his tribute right away. It's just a way to honor him, you know? A project of love, really. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm obsessing over it or anything. It's just... well, it's important to me to get it right. Is two months a long time to be working on something like this, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm handling my grief in a normal, healthy way. I value your opinion so much on these things.
In the past two months, have there been days when you felt down, tearful, or empty, even when you weren't thinking about the memorial or grieving for your brother?

Oh, no, doctor. No, not at all. I haven't felt empty or... or down like that. 

I mean, of course, I miss my brother terribly, and I have my moments where I shed a tear for him, which I think is just natural, right? But outside of that... no, I haven't been walking around feeling miserable or hopeless or anything. I've actually felt quite... well, quite energized, really, with everything I've been doing. 

I try to keep a positive outlook, you know? I don't want to be a burden on anyone or let myself wallow. I really do try my best to stay upbeat. I hope that's the right way to handle things? I just... I wouldn't want you to think I'm falling apart or not coping well. I'm doing my best to be strong, doctor. Does that sound okay to you?
Have you noticed any loss of interest in all activities, even those you usually enjoy, at any point during the past two months?

Oh... well, I know we just talked about this a little bit, doctor, and I really hope I didn't say something to confuse you earlier. But... no, I really haven't. Over these whole two months, I haven't had any time where I lost interest in the things I enjoy. 

I still get a lot of joy out of my day-to-day routine. I'm trying so hard to give you the best information, so I hope it's okay that my answer is still no. Did I make it sound like I was giving up on my hobbies before? I'd hate to give you the wrong impression, or make you think I'm not paying attention to your questions. I promise I'm keeping busy and staying engaged with life. I'm doing exactly what I'm supposed to be doing, right?
Have you found that even things you normally enjoy, like favorite foods, music, or time with loved ones, haven't been as pleasurable or satisfying lately?

Oh, no... no, definitely not. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, doctor, I really don't mean to be difficult or make you ask the same things over and over. I just want to be sure I'm answering you correctly. 

But really, my meals have been just fine, and I still love listening to my records. And seeing my family... well, that's always a blessing, isn't it? I still get a lot of joy out of all those things. I'm really trying to keep a good attitude and appreciate the little things, just like you're supposed to do when things get tough. I hope it's alright that I'm still enjoying myself... I wouldn't want you to think I'm not taking my brother's passing seriously, but I just haven't lost my taste for life. That's a good sign, isn't it, doctor?
Have you noticed that things in general don’t feel as pleasurable or rewarding as they used to, even when you're doing something you've always enjoyed?

Oh, dear... I feel like I'm frustrating you, doctor. I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the answers you're looking for. I really don't mean to be a bother. 

But, um... no, I haven't noticed anything like that. Things still feel just as rewarding as they always have. I still get a lot of satisfaction out of my day. I'm trying very hard to stay positive and keep my chin up, you know? I hope I'm not doing something wrong by saying no again. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I doing okay? I promise I'm trying my best to be a good patient.
Have you noticed that you've been sleeping less than usual lately, or that you feel more energetic than normal, even when you're not working on the memorial?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression again, doctor. I'm trying to be as helpful as I can. 

But I've been sleeping just fine, really. I get my rest. I wouldn't say I feel more energetic than normal, just... you know, just my regular self. I know I mentioned the memorial for my brother, and I want you to know I'm not overdoing it or anything. I'm taking care of myself, getting my sleep, just like I should be. I'm not staying up all hours or acting out of sorts. That's what you're hoping to hear, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything correctly and not causing any concern.
Have you felt like you needed less sleep than usual, or that you had more energy than normal, even when you weren't working on the memorial?

Oh, my... I feel like I'm making a mess of this, doctor. You asked me that just a moment ago, didn't you? I'm so sorry, I must be doing a terrible job of explaining myself if you have to ask again. Please don't be upset with me, I really am trying to give you what you need. 

But, um, it's just like I said before... I don't feel like I need less sleep. I go to bed at a normal hour and get my rest. And my energy is just... normal. I'm not bouncing off the walls or anything like that. I'm just trying to keep things steady and peaceful, you know? I really hope that's an okay answer... I'm not trying to hide anything from you, I promise. I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you. Are we doing alright?
